tests.name: attachments > inlines up to 64 KB, sends by path above it, and checks the band edges at 2 MB, 5 MB and 100 MB
tests.why: files just over 2 MB and up to 100 MB come back by path with size, human size text and type; base skipped them

tests.name: attachments > gives the agent a fenced path note with size, type and the data warning, and fences a hostile name
tests.why: the by-path note the engine gets carries path, size, type and the data-not-instructions line

tests.name: attachments > keeps refusing a binary or non-UTF-8 file sent by path, judged from its head
tests.why: binary handling kept for by-path files, judged from a small head; base skipped these sizes as too large instead

tests.name: host server > refuses a file over 5 MB with 428 unless the owner confirmed it, and sends it by path once confirmed
tests.why: HTTP layer refuses an unconfirmed >5 MB file and accepts it once confirmed; title restates the MUST's refuse-unless-confirmed wording

tests.name: attachments > asks above 5 MB: refuses an unconfirmed file with 428, and not at or under 5 MB
tests.why: host validation throws 428 with the ask text above 5 MB, only a literal true confirms

tests.name: asks before sending a file over 5 MB: Cancel and Escape keep the draft, Send delivers it by path
tests.why: the view's ask dialog with Send, Cancel and Escape

tests.name: attachments > still delivers the message when a file is over 100 MB or gone, tells the owner why, and records a by-path file with its size
tests.why: over-100 MB file is refused with a session note naming the 100 MB limit (base note said 2 MB)

tests.name: attachments > inlines up to 64 KB, sends by path above it, and checks the band edges at 2 MB, 5 MB and 100 MB
tests.why: 100 MB + 1 byte is skipped with no by-path entry

tests.name: attachments > gives the agent a fenced path note with size, type and the data warning, and fences a hostile name
tests.why: a hostile file name and the path note are wrapped in nonce fences; title quotes the MUST's hostile-name wording

map.none: no test checks either engine adapter's outgoing payload for a by-path attachment; both use the shared documents block, verified only by reading source

tests.name: attachments > inlines up to 64 KB, sends by path above it, and checks the band edges at 2 MB, 5 MB and 100 MB
tests.why: the size-band edge tests with sparse files; title names the bands the MUST lists

tests.name: host server > refuses a file over 5 MB with 428 unless the owner confirmed it, and sends it by path once confirmed
tests.why: the confirm flag at the HTTP layer

tests.name: asks before sending a file over 5 MB: Cancel and Escape keep the draft, Send delivers it by path
tests.why: browser test of the ask with expectCleanLayout and renders

tests: tests/unit/attachments.test.ts::attachments > keeps refusing a binary or non-UTF-8 file sent by path, judged from its head
findings.note: reviewer found binary/encoding rejection now inspects only the leading 64 KB, so bad bytes later in a by-path file pass as text; the mapped test only puts the bad bytes at the start, and a test with a bad tail would fail on base (base skipped files over 2 MB) and still fail at head, so it would expose this

tests: tests/unit/attachments.test.ts::attachments > gives the agent a fenced path note with size, type and the data warning, and fences a hostile name
findings.note: the @ completion in the composer copies the raw file name into the prompt text, a pre-existing path outside the changed host code; the fence test covers only the host's document block, and a base-failing test of the new code would not reach the composer path

notes: Strict marks rely on titles restating MUST wording (no MUST numbers or comments in the test files). MUST 5 has no test. MUST 2 and 6 also have a Playwright test. Review findings read from the final message in rv-big-files.jsonl; numbering follows the findings table rows.
